facts.narrative: Rosa, 78, with COPD, used a home oxygen concentrator. During Winter Storm Uri, power went out on February 15 and did not return for two days. Her oxygen machine stopped when power failed and the backup tank ran out the next morning. She died at home on February 17.

# DRAFT: Certifier statement on disaster relationship

> **Draft prepared by Counted for review. Not a death certificate. Not valid until reviewed and signed by the
> certifying medical examiner, coroner or physician.**

| | |
|---|---|
| Case | 629b14862aae |
| Decedent | age 78, female |
| Date of death | 2021-02-17 |
| Location | Harris County, TX |
| Disaster | Winter Storm Uri (DR-4586-TX); incident period 2021-02-11 to 2021-02-21 |
| NWS warnings in force | Dense Fog Advisory (2021-02-10), Winter Storm Watch (2021-02-14), Winter Storm Warning (2021-02-14), Hard Freeze Watch (2021-02-15), Wind Chill Watch (2021-02-15) |
| Cause on certificate (per family) | respiratory failure |

## Determination (CDC 2017 Reference Guide)
In my opinion this death was **indirectly caused** by Winter Storm Uri (DR-4586-TX).

**Causal chain:** Winter Storm Uri caused a prolonged power outage beginning February 15, 2021, in Harris County, TX (DR-4586-TX); loss of electricity disabled the decedent's home oxygen concentrator and exhausted her backup oxygen supply, precipitating respiratory failure in a 78-year-old woman with COPD, resulting in death on February 17, 2021.

**Proposed "How injury occurred" (Item 43):** Winter Storm Uri caused a multi-day power outage beginning 2021-02-15; decedent's home oxygen concentrator ceased functioning and backup oxygen tank was depleted by the morning of 2021-02-16, leaving a COPD-dependent patient without supplemental oxygen for approximately 36 hours prior to death.

**Proposed wording for FEMA Funeral Assistance** (FEMA rejects "may have been caused by"):
> This death was indirectly caused by Winter Storm Uri (DR-4586-TX).

## Family account (verbatim)
- "the power went out on February 15 and did not come back for two days" (loss of utilities)
- "Her oxygen machine stopped when the power failed and the backup tank ran out the next morning" (power dependent medical device)

# Funeral Assistance: what to gather

We are very sorry for your loss. FEMA may help with funeral costs when a death was caused directly or indirectly by a declared disaster.

Good news: FEMA Individual Assistance was approved for Harris County under DR-4586-TX. Funeral Assistance is part of that program.

- [ ] Death certificate, OR the signed certifier statement Counted drafted (ask the medical examiner or doctor to review and sign it)
- [ ] Funeral home contract or itemized receipts
- [ ] Proof of any other help received (insurance, burial societies, donations)
- [ ] The decedent's and applicant's names and addresses

Apply at DisasterAssistance.gov or call 1-800-621-3362. If FEMA says no, you can appeal in writing using the appeal letter below.

## Appeal letter (fill in and sign)

> I am appealing FEMA's decision on Funeral Assistance for __________, who died on 2021-02-17 in Harris County. The enclosed statement from the certifier states the death was indirectly caused by Winter Storm Uri (DR-4586-TX): Winter Storm Uri caused a prolonged power outage beginning February 15, 2021, in Harris County, TX (DR-4586-TX); loss of electricity disabled the decedent's home oxygen concentrator and exhausted her backup oxygen supply, precipitating respiratory failure in a 78-year-old woman with COPD, resulting in death on February 17, 2021.. I ask FEMA to reconsider.

_Counted cannot promise any outcome. FEMA makes the decision._
